The passage covers FENCE and FENCE.TSO, which order data memory and I/O accesses. It never mentions FENCE.I, instruction fetch, or the synchronization needed after writing executable code, so it doesn't answer when FENCE.I is required.

grades.quote: RISC-V does not guarantee that stores to instruction memory will be made visible to instruction fetches on a RISC-V hart until that hart executes a FENCE.I instruction.
grades.reason: Directly answers: stores to instruction memory aren't guaranteed visible to instruction fetches until the hart executes FENCE.I; for other harts, the writer must also do a data FENCE and remote harts must execute FENCE.I.
Discusses reserved fields and the relaxed memory model rationale for data FENCE instructions; does not address FENCE.I or instruction-fetch synchronization.
